## Abstract

Most human papillomaviruses (HPVs) are cutaneous beta- and gamma-types that reside on skin as a commensal reservoir, yet their role in cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (cSCC) remains contested between a "hit-and-run" oncogenic model and a protective-immunity model. Because standard pipelines discard the non-human reads that carry HPV signal, we re-mined public human RNA-seq across skin and related tissues with a uniform pipeline that screens each library for papillomavirus reads, types positives against the full reference panel, and scores productive infection from late (L1 major-capsid) transcript expression. To control the two dominant confounders, we flagged cell-line and engineered material and scored each library as papillomavirus reads-per-million, neutralising sequencing depth. HPV signal was concentrated in non-primary material: cell-line and engineered libraries were roughly five-fold enriched for positivity (OR `r fo(min(stats$cl_or, stats$eng_or))`–`r fo(max(stats$cl_or, stats$eng_or))`, *P* < 10⁻⁸) and dominated by integrated HPV16/HPV18, whereas primary skin carried HPV at only 2–4%. Productive infection was abundant in warts and epidermodysplasia verruciformis (`r round(stats$m3_ctrl_pct)`% of libraries). By contrast, cSCC and actinic keratosis, sequenced almost four times more deeply than the productive controls, reached the control-calibrated detection floor in only `r pp(stats$neo_pctfloor)`% of libraries against `r pp(stats$ctrl_pctfloor)`% of productive controls (Fisher exact OR `r fo(stats$fish_or)`), and their median burden was six orders of magnitude lower. Depth-adjusted, neoplasia did sit above the near-zero baseline of unselected skin (OR `r fo(stats$m2b_or)`, *P* = `r fp(stats$m2b_p)`), but only as a trace footprint (any-read OR `r fo(stats$m2a_or)`, *P* = `r fp(stats$m2a_p)`) that deeper sequencing never converted into productive-level signal. A minority of lesions nonetheless harboured bona fide productive gamma-/alpha-HPV infection (HPV12, HPV96, HPV182, HPV16). Cutaneous HPV is thus productive in warts but transcriptionally quiet in healthy skin and carcinoma: a trace, non-productive footprint that both contested models must accommodate. Beyond HPV, this contamination-aware, depth-normalised framework can mine the discarded fraction of public transcriptomes.

**Keywords:** human papillomavirus; beta-papillomavirus; cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma; skin virome; productive infection; hit-and-run; RNA-seq; public data re-mining; contamination
